conventions.convention: Points form a finite ordered multiset in [0,1)^d, with N≥1; repeated points count with multiplicity. Star discrepancy uses half-open anchored boxes with upper endpoints in [0,1]^d.
Cube integration is bounded Riemann integration on the closed cube. Quadrature averages nodes in the half-open cube; uniform-distribution sequences start at index zero.

Upper-anchor Hardy–Krause variation sums Vitali variations over nonempty coordinate subsets, fixing complementary coordinates at 1. Alternating increments have sign (-1)^(|u|-|ε|). Varied faces with a zero side length have variation zero.
Lower-anchor variation on a subrectangle fixes complementary coordinates at that rectangle's lower endpoints; any varied zero-length side contributes zero.

A base-b (t,m,d)-net has exactly b^m entries and b^t entries in each elementary interval of total depth m-t. Digital matrix constructions use a prime base and acquire a net label only when the counting condition holds.
The smoothness hypothesis includes continuous extensions of all mixed partial derivatives of order at most d and agreement of f's boundary values with its order-zero extension.
The rank-one branch requires N≥1 and gcd(z_1,N)=1. The algorithm permits finite node averages without an integral target when the input function is not bounded Riemann integrable.
The singular transform is g(u)=(1-u)^(-1/2) on [0,1), with g(1)=0. Its finite expectation is a Lebesgue integral, not a bounded Riemann cube integral.

load_bearing.statement: Defines star discrepancy and deterministic cube quadrature for finite nonempty point multisets in [0,1)^d, uniform distribution by vanishing prefix discrepancy, elementary intervals, net counts, and digital constructions.
Upper-anchor Hardy–Krause variation is the sum of Vitali variations of all nonempty face restrictions with complementary coordinates fixed at 1.
Let d≥1 and let f:[0,1]^d→R have finite upper-anchor Hardy–Krause variation. Then f is bounded and Riemann integrable on [0,1]^d.

For a finite nonempty point multiset P in [0,1)^d, finite upper-anchor variation f, and any finite coordinate grid G containing every node coordinate, its lower-corner Riemann sum satisfies |Q_P(f)-S_G(f)|≤D_N*(P)V_HK,1(f).
For every finite nonempty point multiset P in [0,1)^d and f:[0,1]^d→R of finite upper-anchor Hardy–Krause variation, |Q_P(f)-I_d(f)|≤D_N*(P)V_HK,1(f).
A bounded real function on [0,1]^d, d≥1, that is nondecreasing in each coordinate while the others are fixed is Riemann integrable.
Under its stated continuous mixed-partial extension hypothesis, V_HK,1(f) equals the sum over nonempty coordinate subsets u of the integrals of |∂_u f(x_u;1_-u)| on their upper faces.
